**Objects, assumptions, and definitions**

Let \(E\) be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let
\[
d=\dim_{\mathbb R}E\in\mathbb R.
\]
Let \(V:E\to\mathbb R\) and \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Assume:

1. \(0<\alpha\) and \(\alpha\le\beta\).
2. \(V\) is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable.
3. For every \(x,w\in E\),
   \[
   \alpha\|w\|^2
   \le (D(DV)(x)[w])[w]
   \le \beta\|w\|^2.
   \]
4. \(0<d\).

Nonnegative real parameters are coerced to real numbers wherever real arithmetic is displayed below.

Define the state space
\[
S=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times E\times E\times\mathbb N\times E^{\mathbb N}.
\]
Its products are right-associated. Write a state as
\(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\), with \(h:\mathbb N\to E\) a full infinite sequence. Equip this space with the product measurable structure.

For every pair of measurable functions \(\eta,\tau:S\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
\forall s\in S,\quad \eta(s)>0,\qquad \tau(s)>0,
\]
every Markov kernel \(M:S\rightsquigarrow E\), and every threshold
\(\theta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), make the following definitions.

For \(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\), put
\[
v(s)=\frac{\eta(s)+\tau(s)}{\beta+a},
\qquad
a^+(s)=a+\operatorname{toNNReal}(v(s)^{-1}).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{toNNReal}\) truncates a real number below at zero. In these hypotheses \(v(s)>0\), so this truncation does not change the positive inverse.

For \(p=(s,(x,g))\in S\times(E\times E)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
o(p)&=x+\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{\beta+a}}\,g,\\
c(p)&=(a^+(s))^{-1}\bigl(a\,m+v(s)^{-1}o(p)\bigr),\\
F_p(u)&=V(u)+\frac{a^+(s)}2\|u-c(p)\|^2,\\
T_p(u)&=u-(\beta+a^+(s))^{-1}\nabla F_p(u),\\
q(n,p)&=\left\|\nabla F_p\bigl(T_p^{[n]}(x)\bigr)\right\|^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
All scalar-vector products use the real vector-space structure. \(T_p^{[n]}\) denotes \(n\)-fold iteration, including the identity for \(n=0\). The starting point is the newly drawn \(x\), not either stored state coordinate \(m\) or \(b\).

Define
\[
N(p)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q(n,p)\le(\alpha+a^+(s))d\},
 &\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
u(p)=T_p^{[N(p)]}(x).
\]
Define an updated sequence by
\[
h_p^+(0)=o(p),\qquad h_p^+(n+1)=h(n)
\quad(n\in\mathbb N),
\]
and the state update
\[
U(p)=\bigl(a^+(s),c(p),u(p),k+1,h_p^+\bigr).
\]
Thus the observation is prepended to the stored infinite sequence.

Let \(\gamma_E\) be standard Gaussian measure on \(E\). All measures below use the indicated product/Borel structures. All integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals with values in \([0,\infty]\).

**Reconstructed conclusion**

There exists a Markov kernel
\[
J:S\rightsquigarrow E\times S
\]
with the following five properties.

1. **Joint observation and updated-state distribution.** For every \(s\in S\),
   \[
   J(s)=
   \bigl[(x,g)\mapsto(o(s,(x,g)),U(s,(x,g)))\bigr]_{\#}
   \bigl(M(s)\otimes\gamma_E\bigr).
   \]
   The product measure means \(x\) and \(g\) are drawn independently, with respective laws \(M(s)\) and \(\gamma_E\).

2. **First-coordinate marginal.** Writing \(J_1=J.\mathrm{fst}\), for every \(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\in S\),
   \[
   J_1(s)
   =
   [(x,e)\mapsto x+e]_{\#}
   \left(
      M(s)\otimes
      \left[g\mapsto\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{\beta+a}}\,g\right]_{\#}\gamma_E
   \right).
   \]

3. **Exact kernel disintegration identity.** With
   \[
   C=J.\mathrm{condKernel}:
   S\times E\rightsquigarrow S,
   \]
   the equality
   \[
   J_1.\mathrm{compProd}\,C=J
   \]
   holds as an equality of kernels. The operation first draws \(y\) from \(J_1(s)\), then draws the updated state from \(C(s,y)\).

4. **Conditional first two state coordinates.** For every \(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\in S\), for \(J_1(s)\)-almost every \(y\in E\), and then for \(C(s,y)\)-almost every \(t\in S\),
   \[
   t_1=a^+(s)
   \quad\text{and}\quad
   t_2=(a^+(s))^{-1}\bigl(a\,m+v(s)^{-1}y\bigr),
   \]
   where \(t_1\) is the nonnegative-real state coordinate and \(t_2\) is its first \(E\)-coordinate.

5. **Integration identity for every subsequent Markov kernel.** For every Markov kernel \(R:S\rightsquigarrow E\), every \(s\in S\), and every measurable set \(A\subseteq E\),
   \[
   \int_{E\times E}
      R\bigl(U(s,(x,g))\bigr)(A)\,
      d\bigl(M(s)\otimes\gamma_E\bigr)(x,g)
   =
   \int_E
      \left[\int_S R(t)(A)\,dC(s,y)(t)\right]
      dJ_1(s)(y).
   \]

Furthermore, there exists a Markov kernel \(P:S\rightsquigarrow S\) such that, for every \(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\in S\),
\[
P(s)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_s,&\theta\le a,\\
[(x,g)\mapsto U(s,(x,g))]_{\#}
  \bigl(M(s)\otimes\gamma_E\bigr),&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
For every Markov kernel \(R:S\rightsquigarrow E\), every \(s=(a,m,b,k,h)\in S\) satisfying \(a<\theta\), and every measurable set \(A\subseteq E\),
\[
(R.\mathrm{comp}\,P)(s)(A)
=
\int_E
  \left[\int_S R(t)(A)\,dC(s,y)(t)\right]
  dJ_1(s)(y).
\]
Here \(R.\mathrm{comp}\,P\) first draws a state according to \(P(s)\), then an output according to \(R\).

**Quantifier scopes and boundaries**

All assumptions on \(V,\alpha,\beta,E,\eta,\tau\) precede the universal choice of \(M\) and \(\theta\). The existential \(J\) is chosen after those data and before every subsequent universal choice of \(s,R,A\). The same \(J\), its marginal \(J_1\), and its conditional kernel \(C\) appear throughout. The existential \(P\) is also chosen before the final universal choices of \(R,s,A\); neither \(J\) nor \(P\) may be chosen separately for each \(R\) or \(A\).

The displayed marginal and joint distribution equalities hold for every input state, and the disintegration identity is exact as a kernel equality. The coordinate assertion is specifically
\[
\forall s,\quad
\text{for }J_1(s)\text{-a.e. }y,\quad
\text{for }C(s,y)\text{-a.e. }t.
\]
It is not a pointwise assertion for every \(y,t\). Exceptional observation sets may depend on \(s\), and exceptional state sets may depend on \(s,y\). No value of the conditional kernel at an exceptional observation is prescribed by that coordinate assertion. The explicit conditional-coordinate conclusion constrains only the first two coordinates; it does not separately state a conditional formula for the remaining coordinates.

The definition of \(N\) includes a fallback to zero when the stopping predicate has no witness. The conclusion does not separately assert existence of such a witness, a bound on \(N\), or the gradient inequality at \(u(p)\). These must not be added to the reconstructed conclusion merely from the definition.

The final composition identity is conditional on \(a<\theta\). For \(a\ge\theta\), including equality, \(P(s)=\delta_s\); the displayed final identity is not asserted there. If \(\theta=0\), no state has \(a<\theta\), so that conditional clause is vacuous, and \(P\) is the identity/Dirac transition at every state.

No distributional constraint on \(M(s)\) beyond being a Markov probability kernel is assumed. No approximation error, invariant law, convergence rate, or source-paper theorem is claimed.
